policy_notes.note: HUD 2026 Budget Management Letter: vouchers are funding-constrained. PHAs asked to stop issuing new vouchers (except HUD-VASH and FYI), pause new project-based voucher commitments, and cut payment standards, ending exception payment standards and staying inside the 90-110% basic range. Expect payment standards toward the low end of the range.
NSPIRE inspections for vouchers delayed to 2027-02-01 (third extension). Until then PHAs may still inspect under the old HQS (24 CFR 982.401). The checklist here aims at both.

Emergency Housing Vouchers are ending: families under EHV HAP contracts on 2026-09-30 move to Tenant Protection Vouchers by 2026-12-31 (PIH 2026-25); closeout from early 2027. For a landlord the lease continues as an ordinary voucher.
PHAs may use HCV admin fees for landlord signing/retention bonuses, security and utility deposits and holding fees (PIH 2022-18). Optional and per PHA; 2026 budget pressure makes them scarcer.

reasons: City permit/licence required: Yes: every STR (under 30 days) registers yearly and passes an inspection (Ch. 56 Art. VIII, Sec. 56-803).
Primary-residence rule (no investor whole-home STR): Only 'resident' STRs (host lives there 270+ days a year) are allowed in residential zones.
Zoning limits: Non-resident STRs are banned in residential zones unless grandfathered (permitted before June 15 2023); resident STRs are allowed there and exempt from density rules.
Caps/density: Non-resident STRs: 1,000 ft spacing for 1-2 unit buildings; at most 12.5% of units in 3+ unit buildings; none on city-incentivized property.

permit.value: Yes: every STR (under 30 days) registers yearly and passes an inspection (Ch. 56 Art. VIII, Sec. 56-803).

primary_residence.value: Only 'resident' STRs (host lives there 270+ days a year) are allowed in residential zones.

zones.value: Non-resident STRs are banned in residential zones unless grandfathered (permitted before June 15 2023); resident STRs are allowed there and exempt from density rules.

caps.value: Non-resident STRs: 1,000 ft spacing for 1-2 unit buildings; at most 12.5% of units in 3+ unit buildings; none on city-incentivized property.

max_occupancy.value: Registered STRs may hold at most two people per bedroom being rented plus one more per unit, and never more than eight guests per dwelling unit; no food service and no event or party use.

taxes.value: 7.5% transient boarding and accommodation tax, filed quarterly.

listing_id.value: Yes: the STR registration number must appear on all listings.

pending.value: None found in the codified STR article (Ch. 56 Art. VIII, current to Oct 21 2026); no pending amendment was checked on the council docket.

state_preemption.value: No state STR preemption law: an official statute search for 'short-term rental' returns only an unrelated tax section (RSMo 137.018). Pending bills not checked.
